reason: The cited evidence supports that creep in HEAs transitions between diffusion- and dislocation-controlled regimes (E2) and that nanoindentation is used for HEA creep studies (E3), but none of the cited passages provide evidence for the effects of multilayer interfaces on dislocation motion, diffusion, or stress partitioning, which are the core premises of the hypothesis.
premises: Multilayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation glide and climb
Multilayer interfaces hinder atomic diffusion pathways
Creep mechanism transitions from diffusion- to dislocation-controlled with increased stress/temperature
Nanoindentation can characterize time-dependent deformation in HEAs
